I desire 30 multiple choice inquiries with their model answer beneath each inquiry that encompass various facets of the subsequent: The Hair  
- It comprises of:  
a- Shaft: extending above the surface of the dermis.  
b- Root: fixed into the dermis and comprises of:  
1- Inner medulla: polyhedral cells devoid of pigments and contains soft keratin.  
2- Middle cortex: elongated cells with melanin pigments which provide the shade of the hair and contains hard keratin.  
3- Outer cuticle: flat cells containing hard keratin.  
c- Bulb: the enlarged lower end of the hair accountable for its elongation.  
d- Hair follicle:  
* It is a tubular covering formed by an epidermal down growth in which the root of the hair is present.  
* The wall of the hair follicle is referred to as root sheath which is partitioned into 3 types:  
1- Inner root sheath: formed of 3 layers from inside outwards:  
a) Cuticle: flat scales containing soft keratin.  
b) Huxley’s layer: formed of 1-3 layers of cubical cells.  
c) Henle’s layer: formed of one layer of elongated non-nucleated cells.  
2- Outer root sheath: it is similar to the Malpighian layer of the epidermis.  
3- C.T sheath: it is deemed part of C.T. of the dermis and separated from the outer root sheath by a glassy membrane.  

The Sweat glands  
They are located deep in the dermis.  
They are simple coiled tubular glands.  
They are two categories:  
1 - Eccrine sweat glands:  
They are plentiful throughout the dermis of both thick and thin skin.  
Highest concentration in the palms, soles, forehead.  
Composed of secretory portion and excretory ducts.  
A- Secretory portion:  
Located in deep dermis, lined by 2 types of cells:  
a) Dark cells: pyramidal cells that line the lumen of the secretory portion, generate mucous secretion.  
b) Clear cells: positioned between dark cells, release a watery secretion.  
B- Duct portion:  
Lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium.  
Leaves the secretory portion as a coiled duct, then becomes straight.  
Spirals through the epidermis to deliver sweat to the exterior.  
2- Apocrine sweat glands:  
• They differ from the regular eccrine sweat glands in the subsequent:  
Open into the upper part of hair follicles above the entrance of the sebaceous duct.  
Located in the axilla, areola, peri-anal and pubic regions.  
They secrete after puberty (due to the influence of sex hormones).  
Despite their designation, apocrine, they are merocrine glands.  

The Sebaceous glands  
Simple or branched alveolar glands.  
It is a holocrine gland.  
Present over the majority of the body surface except for palms and soles.  
Most numerous and most productive on the scalp, face, and upper back.  
Regulated by androgen hormone.  
Composed of:  
A- Secretory portion:  
• Composed of acini embedded in the dermis.  
• The acinus is formed of larger cells filled with lipid vacuoles which degenerate to form an oily product known as sebum.  
• Sebum is discharged into the sebaceous duct, which opens into the upper part of the hair follicle.  
• Sebum acts as cream that helps to maintain skin pliable preventing its cracking.  
B- Duct portion: is lined by stratified squamous epithelium.  

The Arrector pili muscles  
• Also termed as hair erector muscles, they are small muscles connected to hair follicles.  
• Contraction of these muscles causes the hairs to be in an upright position (standing).  
• Each arrector pili is comprised of a bundle of smooth muscle fibers.

* The wall of the hair follicle is called root sheath which is subdivided into 3 types:  
1- Inner root sheath: composed of 3 layers from inside outwards:  
a) Cuticle: flat scales containing soft keratin.  
b) Huxley’s layer: composed of 1-3 layers of cubical cells.  
c) Henle’s layer: composed of a single layer of elongated non-nucleated cells.  
2- Outer root sheath: it is identical to the Malpighian layer of the epidermis.  
3- C.T sheath: it is regarded as part of C.T. of the dermis and is separated from the outer root sheath by a glassy membrane.  

The Sweat glands  
They are found deep in the dermis.  
They are simple coiled tubular glands.  
They are two categories:  
1 - Eccrine sweat glands:  
They are plentiful throughout the dermis of both thick and thin skin.  
Highest concentration in the palms, soles, forehead.  
Consisting of a secretory section and excretory ducts.  
A- Secretory section:  
Located in deep dermis, lined by 2 categories of cells:  
a) Dark cells: pyramidal cells that line the lumen of the secretory section, produce mucous secretion.  
b) Clear cells: placed between dark cells, release a watery secretion.  
B- Duct section:  
Lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium.  
Leaves the secretory section as a coiled duct, then becomes straight.  
Spirals through the epidermis to deliver sweat to the outside.  
2- Apocrine sweat glands:  
• They differ from the typical eccrine sweat glands in the following:  
Open into the upper portion of hair follicles above the entrance of the sebaceous duct.  
Located in axilla, areola, peri-anal and pubic regions.  
They secrete following puberty (Due to the influence of sex hormones).  
Despite their name, apocrine, they are merocrine glands.  

The Sebaceous glands  
Simple or branched alveolar glands.  
It is a holocrine gland.  
Present over the majority of the body surface except for palms and soles.  
Most numerous and most productive on the scalp, face, and upper back.  
Controlled by androgen hormone.  
Composed of:  
A- Secretory portion:  
• Formed of acini embedded in the dermis.  
• The acinus is composed of larger cells filled with lipid vacuoles which degenerate to form an oily product referred to as sebum.  
• Sebum is discharged into the sebaceous duct, which opens into the upper section of the hair follicle.  
• Sebum serves as cream that aids in maintaining skin soft and preventing its cracking.  
B- Duct portion: is lined by stratified squamous epithelium.  

The Arrector pili muscles  
• Also known as hair erector muscles, they are small muscles connected to hair follicles.  
• Contraction of these muscles causes the hairs to be in erect position (standing).  
• Each arrector pili is made up of a bundle of smooth muscle fibers.
